title: Origin and Consequences of Sin
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Temptation is taught with hope: being tempted is not sin (Hebrews 4:15; 1 Corinthians 10:13).

skills.key_step: The learner explains the origin of sin (Genesis 3: the serpent's doubt, desire, disobedience) and examines its consequences (shame and hiding, blame, broken relationships, pain and toil, death, being sent from the garden).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the story of the fall.
floor.question: Who tempted Eve?

board.do: Draw four broken links: with God, each other, self, creation.

board.say: How did sin break this relationship in Genesis 3?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say they hid from God.

listen_for: The fruit of the tree of life
misconceptions.ask: What had God forbidden Adam and Eve to eat?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 2:16-17 and 3:6: the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

misconceptions.ask: Who tempted Eve in the garden?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 3:1 and James 1:13: the serpent tempted; God tempts no one.

misconceptions.ask: Name a consequence of the fall in Genesis 3.
misconceptions.repair: List consequences in Genesis 3:14-24: shame, fear, pain, toil, broken relationships, death, sent from the garden.

misconceptions.ask: What did Adam and Eve do when they heard God walking in the garden (Genesis 3:8)?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 3:8-10 and ask why they hid: shame and fear replaced friendship with God.

checks.question: Name a consequence of the fall.
checks.answer: Sent out of the garden (shame, toil, pain, death)

skills.key_step: The learner analyses causes of sin today (own desires, peer pressure, media, greed, pride, idleness, drugs) and names values and life skills to overcome temptation (self-control, assertiveness, decision-making, watchfulness and prayer, good company), with James 1:13-15 and 1 Corinthians 10:13.

floor.question: How did Jesus answer the devil in Luke 4?

representations: a chart: temptation, way out, skill
steps: Plan a way out for a temptation.
contexts: an exam with a chance to cheat
a phone at night with harmful sites

board.do: Draw a chain: desire, temptation, sin, death (James 1:14-15).
Point at the link between temptation and sin.
board.say: Where can this chain be broken?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say at temptation, with God's way out.
Fill in the chart of temptations and ways out.

listen_for: Yes, God tempts us to see if we fall
misconceptions.ask: According to James 1:13, does God tempt anyone to do evil?
misconceptions.repair: Read James 1:13-14. Tell testing from tempting: God allows trials, but never pushes to sin.

listen_for: The devil is fully to blame
misconceptions.ask: Juma steals and says "the devil made me do it". What does James 1:14 teach?
misconceptions.repair: Link with Genesis 3:12-13 (blaming) and James 1:14 (own desire). Own the choice and repent.

misconceptions.ask: What does 1 Corinthians 10:13 promise about temptation?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Corinthians 10:13 and plan a "way out" for three common temptations.

listen_for: Yes, being tempted is already sin
misconceptions.ask: Is it a sin to be tempted?
misconceptions.repair: Read Hebrews 4:15: Jesus was tempted in every way, yet without sin.

checks.question: According to James 1:13, does God tempt anyone?
Name a life skill that helps overcome temptation.
